- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "Noumena" refers to the thing-in-itself, or the true reality that exists independent of our perception of it, as discussed in Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "A priori" refers to knowledge that is independent of experience, as discussed in Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "A posteriori" refers to knowledge that is dependent on experience, as discussed in Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "Synthetic judgments" are judgments that go beyond the concepts contained within them and introduce new information, as discussed in Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "Analytic judgments" are judgments that are true by virtue of the concepts contained within them and do not introduce new information, as discussed in Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason."
